messages:
Oliver: Hey team — enterprise POC (FinLedger) just asked for a committed throughput plan. They want reserved GPUs + autoscale and clear failover behavior. Can eng help size?
Kevin: Quick q — what's their 95th pct RPS during sync windows? Dana: They gave a spike profile: baseline 120 req/s, 5m spike to 800 req/s every 4 hours for batch settlements.
Maria: For those spikes I'd recommend reserved GPU pool sized for steady baseline and a burst policy for the spikes. Reserved for baseline = ~120 req/s -> 2 x A10s (conservative).
Kevin: 2 A10s for baseline seems high — what's our per-GPU token throughput assumption?
Maria: Using our chart: A10 ~ 250-300 small-gen requests/sec for short seq (<512). For their mixed prompts let's assume 200 req/s per GPU. So baseline 120 -> 1 GPU technically, but we recommend 2 for headroom + KV cache hit variance.
Oliver: They want formal numbers for contract. Can we show a cost comparison: reserved 2 GPUs + burst credits vs reserving 4 GPUs?
Sam: Yes. Option A: reserved 2 + burst (auto-burst to shared capacity) with prewarm policy; Option B: reserved 4 dedicated. Provide expected latency SLOs for each.
Dana: Also need autoscale config snippet so their infra/ops understands behavior. Example:
```
autoscale:
  min_replicas: 2
  max_replicas: 8
  scale_up_threshold: 0.75  # scale when 75% GPU util
  cool_down: 45s
  burst_policy:
    enabled: true
    fallback_pool: shared-burst
    prewarm: true
```
Kevin: Important: prewarm should start ~60s before expected spike to avoid cold-start latency. For scheduled spikes we can prewarm via a cron hook.
Maria: Failure modes: if shared-burst is exhausted, route to fallback model variant (lower-cost quantized) — document that as graceful degradation.
Oliver: They asked about billing during burst — are burst tokens charged at on-demand rate or a special rate?
Sam: Burst usage on Redwood Dedicated is billed as overage at on-demand rate per GPU-minute. For enterprise we can negotiate a blended burst rate and burst-credit pool in contract.
Dana: Security question: if we route to shared-burst, we must ensure data isolation for their regulated workload. Can we guarantee that request data never hits other customers' models?
Maria: Yes — routing to shared-burst still uses tenant isolation. We log in audit trail: model_variant and pool used. For strict isolation customer can require dedicated fallback pool (adds cost).
Oliver: Can we give a single-slide summary for sales: recommended reserve, burst policy, expected monthly cost delta, and failure plan?
Kevin: I'll draft numbers. Quick calc: baseline 2 reserved A10s (~$Xk/month), expected burst minutes ~ 40m/day -> adds Y GPU-min/day at on-demand. Will convert to monthly.
deploy-bot: deploy status: reserved-pool-config v2 applied to staging at 1938645201 :rocket:
Dana: Nice. Last asks: SLA implications if fallback to quantized model — do we document quality delta?
Maria: Yes include an eval summary: latency vs quality tradeoff and example prompts where quantized variant may alter outputs. Add canary % (5-10%) before full fallback.
Oliver: Great — please drop the slide and the concise runbook here by EOD so I can send to FinLedger. @Kevin @Maria @Sam thanks. :thumbsup:
